title: Provider protocol messages
description: Draft 0.2. Every line exchanged between kernel and provider is one of these messages. Top-level objects accept extra fields under an x- prefix; nested objects are closed. Bulk data never travels in a message: files are referred to by relative path in the working directory of the request, with their identity. Below protocol 1.0 there is no compatibility promise. Schema validation is a first filter. The kernel also applies the rules in protocol/README.md that a schema cannot express.

id.description: Chosen by the kernel, unique within a session. The answer carries the same id.

file_ref.description: A file in the working directory of the request, by relative path, with the identity of its bytes. Bulk data never travels in a message; this is how it is referred to.

name.description: Optional: the definition, artifact or other node this file materialises.

tool_tree.description: A pinned tool tree made available to the request.

name.description: Tool name as in the lock.

root.description: Directory in the working directory that holds the pinned tool tree. Absent when the tree is not placed there and exists only where runs are executed; a run description then names its files as ${tool:NAME}/PATH.

listing.description: The files of the tree, as protocol/tool-tree-digest.md describes a listing, so that a provider can name a file of the tool without the tree being in its working directory.

evidence_link.description: The three evidence links of MODEL.md section 5: specification to code, code to what runs, what runs to the world.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

rejected.description: Every file the provider could not index, with a reason code. A file is never dropped silently.

identity.description: A function of content alone: never of time, location or machine (decision 0004).

depends_on.description: Names this definition depends on, sorted by UTF-8 bytes. Names are scoped by the binding that indexed them. A dependency on a name indexed by another binding is not decided.

granularity.description: The granularity actually achieved for this definition.

files.description: Files that materialise the definition for a tool to read, sorted by UTF-8 bytes.

obligation.description: One obligation as enumerated by a provider (MODEL.md section 3).

name.description: Stable locator within the binding. Survives edits to the content.

kind.description: reproducibility obligations are derived by the kernel and never enumerated by a provider.

defect_of.description: For a planted defect: the name, in the same binding, of the obligation whose check it must break. Present exactly when expect is violated.

config.description: Bounds, flags, seeds, worker counts and limits. Provider-defined; integers, strings, booleans, arrays and objects only, no floating point. The kernel hashes it into the core key.

inputs.description: The paths of the files a check of this obligation may read, sorted, each one of the files the request listed. The host gives a check these files and no others; a check that needs a file not listed cannot read it, which ends in an error, never a pass.

obligation_in_check.description: The obligation to decide, as the provider enumerated it, with its binding.

defect_of.description: For a planted defect: the name, in the same binding, of the obligation whose check it must break. Present exactly when expect is violated.

wall_ms.description: Longest the run may take, in milliseconds on a monotonic clock.

run_description.description: What to run (decision 0007). A verifier describes a run; it never starts one.

program.description: The program to start, as a relative path inside a pinned tool tree.

tool.description: Name of a tool in the pinned closure.

path.description: Exact file inside that tool's tree.

args.description: Argument list. Never a string meant for a shell. An argument may name a file inside a pinned tool tree as ${tool:NAME}/PATH; the executor replaces that with where the file is on its machine.

inputs.description: Input files in the run's working directory, sorted by path.

directory.description: The output is a directory. Everything in it comes back, described as a listing in the report.

outputs.description: Output files the run is expected to leave, sorted by path. A missing non-optional output is an error.

tools.description: Digests of every tool in the closure the run expects, including runtimes, sorted by name. The executor reports what it actually ran; any difference is an error.

env.description: Environment variables for the program, complete: nothing is inherited. A value may refer to the root of a pinned tool tree as ${tool:NAME} and to the working directory as ${work}. The program starts in the working directory.

cwd.description: Directory the program starts in, relative to the run's working directory. The working directory itself when absent.

run_report.description: The executor's final report on a run. The kernel compares platform and tools_ran with the run description; a difference is an error, never a result.

handle.description: The executor's handle for the run.

end.description: How the run ended. unavailable means the executor could not run it at all, and the check ends unavailable; anything else but exited ends the check in error. The provider is not asked to interpret a run that did not exit.

platform.description: The platform the run actually executed on.

captured_output.description: The raw captured output. Its identity is the output digest in the evidence record.

outputs.description: The declared output files that exist, by relative path and identity.

final_check.description: A final verdict. strength is required for passed and failed. A final of passed or failed with no run behind it is refused by the kernel: a verdict must rest on at least one run. The strength may not exceed the one the manifest declares, in rank or class; a final that does is refused (conformance/README.md, Host checks).

verdict.description: The verdicts a provider may give. pending and unavailable are never the provider's to give.

trusted_base.description: Assumptions specific to this result, such as axioms a proof used.

summary.description: Provider-defined. Only fields the manifest lists as comparable are compared across platforms.

attachments.description: Logs, counterexamples and diagnostics. A failure found by a tool carries its counterexample here.

final_build.description: Final result of a build. The manifest gives artifact.build no strength, so none is carried here.

verdict.description: The verdicts a provider may give. pending and unavailable are never the provider's to give.

trusted_base.description: Assumptions specific to this result, such as axioms a proof used.

summary.description: Provider-defined. Only fields the manifest lists as comparable are compared across platforms.

attachments.description: Logs, counterexamples and diagnostics. A failure found by a tool carries its counterexample here.

outputs.description: Build outputs by relative path and identity. Each becomes an artifact node named by the producing obligation and the path.

deterministic.description: Whether this build is byte-identical on repeat. Honoured only if the manifest allows artifact reproducibility.

declared.description: Further inputs the provider declares. Allowed only in the answer that carries the first run of a check; the evidence key is fixed when that run is submitted. Later runs may name only tools and inputs already in the key.

run_result_request.description: Sent by the kernel after a run described by next has ended. The output files named in the report are in the working directory. Sent only when the run ended as exited. A run that timed out, was cancelled or exceeded a limit ends the check in error and the provider is not asked.

check.description: The id of the request that started this check. Several checks may be in flight in one session.

run.description: Which run of the check this is, counting from 1. The key under which the kernel submits a run includes this number, so a repeated run is never answered from an earlier one.

inputs.description: Materialised inputs: specification and target files, and input artifacts, sorted by path.

tools.description: Pinned tool trees available, sorted by name.

platform.description: The platform the run will target.

inputs.description: Materialised inputs: specification and target files, and input artifacts, sorted by path.

tools.description: Pinned tool trees available, sorted by name.

platform.description: The platform the run will target.

mapping.description: Files that map the specification onto the implementation, with their identities.

oneOf.description: Run this, then send the report back as a run.result request.

check_result.description: Exactly one of next or final.

oneOf.description: Run this, then send the report back as a run.result request.

build_result.description: Exactly one of next or final.

oneOf.description: Run this, then send the report back as a run.result request.

conformance_result.description: Exactly one of next or final.

items.description: An obligation that checks this criterion.

varying.description: Declared in advance for a check on something that varies: how many runs, and how many must agree (decision 0018). agree is at most runs.

links.description: checked-by links, sorted by binding then obligation. An empty list means the criterion is uncovered.

condition.description: Deferred gates only: what is to be observed, in plain words.

limit_days.description: Deferred gates only: days after the intent is first reported delivered by which the observation must be made. The kernel derives the due date; no date takes part in identity.

not_applicable.description: Evidence links the owner declared not applicable. Honoured only in a confirmed baseline.

intent.description: An intent as read from a file. The kernel computes the intent's identity from these fields over the canonical encoding (protocol/canonical-encoding.md); the provider does not supply one. A provider never reports that an intent is confirmed: confirmation comes only from an act record with a ticket the kernel issued.

text.description: The intent as written, all of it: what an owner confirms. Changing any of it changes the baseline.

worker.description: Who does the work the intent asks for, when the file says.

touches.description: What the intent expects to touch: definition names or path prefixes, sorted.

amendment.description: A recorded change to criteria or gates (decision 0020). The separation level of the act is computed by the kernel from the act record, never taken from here.

what.description: Which part changed, as a path such as criteria/2/gate.

granted_by.description: Who granted it. The kernel checks that this is the intent's owner; the act record, not this field, decides how separate the grantor was.

identity.description: Hash of the record, chosen by the provider as a function of content alone.

status.description: The provider maps its own vocabulary onto these four (decision 0001).

identity.description: The identity the governed name had when the decision was written.

obligations.description: Every obligation the project's bindings enumerated, sorted by binding then name, so the provider can say which obligations check each criterion. Absent or empty when there are none.

req_obligation_enumerate.description: The binding and its indexed definitions, with the materialising files in the working directory.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

rejected.description: Definitions the provider could not turn into an obligation, with a reason code.

key.description: Identifies the submission. A repeated submission with the same key is the same run.

req_run_submit.description: Executor requests. An executor that cannot run a request answers with an error whose code is unavailable (or unsupported); there is no fallback.

oneOf.description: Answer to poll or cancel: the run has ended.
Answer to cancel: the run was stopped. The report has end cancelled.

tree_into.description: If present, also place the tree here in the working directory.

digest.description: Digest of the tool tree for this platform.

entry.description: Optional entry point inside the tree.

tree.description: Where the tree was placed, when asked for.

oneOf.description: no-build-for-platform makes the obligations that need it unsupported on that platform.

protocol.description: Protocol versions the kernel speaks. The provider picks one and names it in its manifest.

max_line_bytes.description: A longer line ends the session.

deadline_ms.description: Time the provider has to answer hello, in milliseconds on a monotonic clock.

echo.description: A string with non-ASCII and control characters (escaped in JSON). The provider returns it unchanged in its manifest answer, so an encoding fault ends the session before any work.

deadline_ms.description: Time the provider has to answer, in milliseconds on a monotonic clock, counted from when the kernel sent the line. An answer after it is logged and dropped.

code.description: unsupported gives the check the verdict unsupported, unavailable the verdict unavailable, the others error.
